subject: Information Theory
title: Repetition Codes
description: A quick, practical guide to Repetition Codes.

hook.text: Send each bit three times: 0 becomes 000, 1 becomes 111. Majority vote fixes one flip. Crude but effective.

buildup.text: A repetition code with rate 1/n sends each bit n times. The decoder takes the majority vote.

discovery.text: The (3,1) code corrects 1 error. The (5,1) code corrects 2. But the rate plummets—only 1/n is useful data.

twist.text: Repetition codes are the worst efficient codes possible. They waste the most bandwidth for the least correction.

climax.text: They prove a concept: redundancy enables correction. Real codes do the same job with far less overhead.

punchline.text: Say it three times. Vote. Fixed. But very wasteful.

quiz.question: Why are repetition codes inefficient?
options: They use extreme redundancy for minimal correction
